phases.title: Phase 0 — Monolith Scaffold
phases.tagline: Auth, Orders, Payments, Vault, infra — the skeleton everything hangs on.
phases.recall: If you forget everything else, remember this: Merchant owns everything. Order groups attempts. Payment moves through a state machine. Vault keeps raw cards out of your DB.
howto: docker compose -f services.docker-compose.yaml up -d postgres redis

phases.title: Phase 1 — Idempotency
phases.tagline: Same POST twice with the same key = one charge, one replayed response.
phases.recall: Filter runs before controllers. Key scope is merchantId:key. IN_PROGRESS (30s) blocks doubles, COMPLETED (24h) replays the saved response.
howto: Retry same request → identical response, no second charge

phases.title: Phase 2 — Customer + 4 Rate Limiters
phases.tagline: findOrCreate customer on every order + swappable abuse protection.
phases.recall: Customer is keyed by (merchantId, email) — auto-created inside createOrder. Rate limiter is one interface, 4 beans, chosen by app.rate-limit.method (fixed active). ApiKey filter enforces 100/min.
howto: POST /api/orders with { customer: { email, name, phone } } → customer row reused
Set app.rate-limit.method: sliding-lua → restart → atomic Lua limiting

phases.title: Phase 3 — Outbox + Webhook Config (committed)
phases.commit: a7dc102 · Webhook and outbox has been added
phases.tagline: Payments publish reliably to Kafka; merchants choose which events hit their URL.
phases.recall: publish() saves OutboxEvent in the SAME DB transaction as the payment. OutboxPoller (5s) forwards to Kafka. MerchantWebhookConfig stores targetUrl + secret + event filter. Kafka topics: payments/orders/refunds/settlements.events.
howto: Create/capture a payment → row in outbox_event → Kafka payments.events

phases.title: Phase 4 — Webhook Delivery + DLQ (YOU ARE HERE)
phases.tagline: Kafka → signed POST with retries → dead-letter when hopeless. Written, not yet committed.
phases.recall: Consumer looks up active configs, HMAC-signs payload (SignerUtil), saves WebhookEvent PENDING, pushes to Redis ZSET. Scheduler (1s poll + 10s DB reconcile) delivers on virtual threads. 7 tries: 1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h, 24h → DEAD + DlqEvent. FIX BEFORE COMMIT: re-add worktree (package com.example…), Lombok on entities, fix trusted.packages in application.yaml:40.
howto: git add -A && git commit -m 'Webhook delivery pipeline'
Test: POST to DummyMerchantWebhookController → watch attempts column grow

phases.title: Phase 5 — Next Up (not started)
phases.tagline: Uncomment, fill in, expose: simulator, order events, refunds, settlements, DLQ replay.
phases.recall: 1) Uncomment @Scheduled in BankCallbackSimulator:24. 2) Uncomment ORDER_CREATED/CANCELLED publish in OrderServiceImpl:68,100. 3) Build RefundService. 4) Build SettlementService + scheduler. 5) DLQ replay API (replayedAt is never set today).
howto: Start with the simulator — without it async authorize never resolves
Then order events — one-line uncomment each

nodes.label: Auth
nodes.body: Dual auth. Signup hashes with BCrypt, login returns JWT (JwtUtil). API keys go through ApiKeyAuthenticationFilter: X-API-Key → RedisApiKeyCache → MerchantContext ThreadLocal. WebSecurityConfig chains both filters.
nodes.recall: MerchantContext holds merchantId per request — every query is merchant-scoped.

nodes.label: Rate Limit
nodes.body: One RateLimiter interface, four beans switched by app.rate-limit.method: fixed (active), sliding, sliding-lua (atomic, best), bucket. Enforced inside the ApiKey filter at 100/min → 429 with X-RateLimit-* headers. Fail-open on Redis outage.
nodes.recall: To compare algorithms, just flip one YAML key and restart.

nodes.label: Idempotency
nodes.body: OncePerRequestFilter on POST/PUT/PATCH. Claims merchantId:key via setIfAbsent. IN_PROGRESS=30s blocks concurrent doubles; COMPLETED=24h replays the cached response body. Conflict → 409.

nodes.label: Customer
nodes.body: Keyed by (merchantId, email). Auto-created inside createOrder when request.customer is present. No dedicated controller — lives under orders.
nodes.recall: Same email + same merchant = same row, always.

nodes.label: Orders
nodes.body: OrderController create/get/cancel/listPayments. Receipt must be unique per merchant (DuplicateResourceException). expiresAt = +30m. NOTE: ORDER_CREATED / ORDER_CANCELLED outbox publish is commented out (OrderServiceImpl:68,100) — orders emit nothing today.
nodes.recall: Uncomment two lines to put orders on the event bus.

nodes.label: Payments
nodes.body: initiate → ATTEMPTED → gateway router (Card/UPI/NetBanking adapters + processor strategies) → Pending/Success/Failure. capture uses pessimistic lock. Every transition writes PaymentTransitionLog. resolveAuthorization auto-captures. Publishes PAYMENT_CREATED / PAYMENT_STATUS_CHANGED via outbox.
nodes.recall: State machine is the source of truth; gateway result is just input.

nodes.label: Bank Simulator
nodes.body: Fakes bank latency/success-rate per method + ChaosMode. BUT @Scheduled is commented out (BankCallbackSimulator:24) so processCallbacks() never runs — async authorizations hang. First backlog item: uncomment it.
nodes.recall: Without this, Pending payments never resolve.

nodes.label: Vault
nodes.body: PAN never touches payment tables. AES-GCM with vault.master-key encrypts → token returned. Detokenize only inside Vault. ExpiryYear validator guards input.
nodes.recall: PCI boundary: raw cards stop here.

nodes.label: Outbox
nodes.body: OutboxEventPublisher.publish() saves the event in the same DB transaction as the payment — no lost events on crash. OutboxPoller every 5s sends PENDING rows to Kafka (idempotent producer). Gap: no SKIP LOCKED, so multi-instance can double-send.

nodes.label: Kafka
nodes.body: KRaft single-broker (confluent-local:7.5.0). Topics: payments/orders/refunds/settlements.events. Manual ack, earliest offset. UI at :9021 Control Center.

nodes.label: Webhook Config
nodes.body: Merchants register targetUrl + secret + event filter (ALL or CSV) via WebhookConfigController. MerchantWebhookApi.getActiveConfigsForEvent() is what the consumer calls per event.
nodes.recall: Secret per config → per-target HMAC signature.

nodes.label: Delivery
nodes.body: Consumer persists WebhookEvent PENDING + enqueues in Redis ZSET (score=retryAt). Scheduler: 1s pollDue → virtual-thread deliver; 10s reconcile PENDING from DB. Executor POSTs with X-Razorpay-Signature, backoff 1m→24h, max 7 attempts.
nodes.recall: Redis is the timer, Postgres is the truth.

nodes.label: DLQ
nodes.body: WebhookDlqRecorder marks event DEAD and writes DlqEvent (finalError + payload). No replay API yet — replayedAt is never set. Next: POST /api/dlq/{id}/replay.
nodes.recall: Dead doesn't mean gone — it means waiting for replay.

nodes.label: Refund/Settle
nodes.body: Only entities exist (Refund, Settlement, SettlementPayment). No service, repo query, scheduler, or controller. Settlement math: net = gross − refunds − fee − GST.

nodes.label: Infra
nodes.body: services.docker-compose.yaml: postgres:18, redis:7 (appendonly), kafka KRaft + control-center. app.yaml: ddl-auto update, virtual threads on, fixed rate-limit, delivery redis-key webhook-retry batch 100.
nodes.recall: docker compose up -d is step zero of every demo.

meta.howToExtend: To add a phase: append an entry to phases[] in journey.json with matching node ids, then push — GitHub Pages redeploys automatically. Anchors #/phase-4 deep-link each card.

tech.name: PostgreSQL 18
tech.why: System of record: merchants, API keys, orders, payments, outbox, webhooks, settlements all live as JPA @Entities. ddl-auto:update while building; jsonb columns carry flexible event payloads.
tech.witty: The truth. If it's not in Postgres, it didn't happen.

tech.name: Redis — API-key cache
tech.why: Every merchant API call authenticates — hitting Postgres + BCrypt each time would melt. apikey:{id} cached 5 min, evicted on revoke/rotate.

tech.name: Redis — rate limiting
tech.why: Counters (INCR + EXPIRE) enforce 100 req/min per API key inside the auth filter. 4 algorithms, one YAML switch; Lua variants make check-and-set atomic.

tech.name: Redis — idempotency store
tech.why: SETNX claims merchantId:key as IN_PROGRESS (30s) then stores the completed response (24h). Double-clicks and retries replay instead of re-charging.

tech.name: Redis — webhook retry queue
tech.why: A sorted set scored by retry timestamp is a delay queue with no extra infra: pollDue = 'everything whose time has come'.

tech.name: Kafka — outbox relay
tech.why: DB is written first, Kafka second (5s poller, idempotent producer, merchantId as key). Crash between the two loses nothing — the row is still PENDING.
tech.witty: The postman. DB writes the letter, Kafka delivers it.

tech.name: Kafka — webhook fan-out
tech.why: One domain event → N merchant deliveries. Manual ack: infra failure = redeliver, logic error = DLQ + ack. Control Center on :9021 to watch it.

tech.name: JWT + API keys (dual auth)
tech.why: Humans get short-lived JWTs (dashboard), machines get revocable keyId.secret pairs with env scoping and grace periods. Two @Order'd chains, stateless sessions.
tech.witty: Humans show ID. Machines show keys.

tech.name: MapStruct + Lombok
tech.why: Compile-time DTO mapping (no reflection) + no boilerplate. Secrets mapped once in mappers, never hand-copied in services.

tech.name: Bean Validation
tech.why: @Valid at every controller + constraints on DTOs (email, Luhn card check, https-only webhook URLs). Bad input dies at the edge as 400.

tech.name: Java 25 virtual threads
tech.why: Webhook POSTs, JPA calls and Kafka sends all block — virtual threads make millions of blocked fibers cheap. Scheduler uses newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor.

tech.name: AES-GCM vault (envelope)
tech.why: Raw PAN never touches payment tables: random data-key encrypts the card, master key encrypts the data-key. PCI blast radius ends here.
tech.witty: Cards go in, tokens come out. Raw numbers never leave.

tech.name: HMAC-SHA256 webhooks
tech.why: Each delivery carries X-Razorpay-Signature over {event,payload} with the merchant's own secret — receivers can prove it came from you.

tech.name: RestClient (3s/5s)
tech.why: Synchronous merchant POSTs with tight connect/read timeouts — slow receivers fail fast into the retry queue instead of clogging deliverers.

tech.name: Inline Lua scripts
tech.why: Token-bucket refill and sliding-window eviction must be atomic — Lua runs check-and-update inside Redis, closing the race plain Java has.

annotations.body: Marks the entry point and turns on auto-configuration + component scanning. Everything under com.example.razorpay gets discovered from here.
annotations.why: One annotation boots the whole monolith; @EnableScheduling and @EnableJpaAuditing sit beside it.
annotations.title: @SpringBootApplication

annotations.body: Declares a class as a factory of beans. Method-level @Bean registers singletons (RestClient, passwordEncoder, processor maps) into the context.
annotations.why: All wiring lives here: security chains, adapter/processor maps, RestClient with 3s/5s timeouts.
annotations.title: @Configuration + @Bean

annotations.body: Injects a value from application.yaml (with :default fallback). Used for secrets, TTLs, rate limits, expiry minutes.
annotations.why: No hardcoded secrets or tunables — change YAML, restart, done.
annotations.title: @Value

annotations.body: Binds a whole YAML subtree to a typed object. KafkaProperties reads app.kafka.*, SimulatorConfig reads payment.simulator.*.
annotations.why: Type-safe config with IDE completion instead of scattered @Value strings.
annotations.title: @ConfigurationProperties

annotations.body: Creates a bean only when app.rate-limit.method matches. Exactly one of the 4 RateLimiter beans exists at runtime.
annotations.why: This is the whole 4-algorithm switch: flip one YAML key, restart, different limiter.
annotations.title: @ConditionalOnProperty

annotations.body: Generic stereotype for singletons with logic (routers, state machine, retry queue, signer). @Service is its domain-logic sibling.
annotations.why: Routers, state machine, SignerUtil are all @Component — infrastructure plumbing, not business services.
annotations.title: @Component / @Service

annotations.body: Orders the two security chains: JWT chain first, API-key chain second. First match wins.
annotations.why: Without @Order the two filter chains would compete unpredictably.
annotations.title: @Order

annotations.body: Runs a method on a fixed delay without cron. Powers the three background loops: outbox relay (5s), webhook dispatch (1s), DB reconcile (10s).
annotations.pitfall: BankCallbackSimulator's @Scheduled is commented out — async authorizations never resolve until you uncomment it.
annotations.why: All async movement in the system is just @Scheduled polling, no message broker magic on the consume side.
annotations.title: @Scheduled

annotations.body: Subscribes a method to Kafka topics. The webhook consumer listens on all 4 domain-event topics with manual ack.
annotations.why: One listener fans one domain event out to N merchant webhook deliveries.
annotations.title: @KafkaListener

annotations.body: Makes a method transactional. Variants used: plain (payment write + outbox in one TX), readOnly (queries), REQUIRES_NEW (DLQ write must survive outer rollback).
annotations.why: Outbox correctness depends on it: payment row + event row commit atomically.
annotations.title: @Transactional

annotations.body: Marks a class as a REST endpoint; method annotations map HTTP verbs to paths. All controllers are thin — they validate and delegate.
annotations.why: Controllers hold zero business logic; services + state machine do the work.
annotations.title: @RestController + mappings

annotations.body: Central error translator: exceptions become clean JSON + status codes (409 duplicate, 404 not found, 429 rate-limit, 400 validation).
annotations.why: Clients never see stack traces — every failure is a typed ErrorResponse.
annotations.title: @RestControllerAdvice

annotations.body: Marks a persistent class. Every table (merchant, payment, outbox_event, webhook_event…) is one @Entity extending BaseEntity audit fields.
annotations.why: BaseEntity gives every row id + created/modified timestamps + actor for free.
annotations.title: @Entity + @MappedSuperclass

annotations.body: Value object without identity. Money (amountUnits + currency) is embedded into Payment, Order, Settlement — never its own table.
annotations.why: Money logic (currency handling) lives in one place, reused across 5+ entities.
annotations.title: @Embeddable / @Embedded

annotations.body: Stores a Map/object as Postgres jsonb instead of a joined table. Event payloads and webhook bodies live in one column.
annotations.why: Flexible event schemas without migrations every time a payload field changes.
annotations.title: @JdbcTypeCode(JSON)

annotations.body: Takes a DB row-lock while reading. Capture and callback load the Payment row FOR UPDATE so two concurrent captures can't double-charge.
annotations.why: The anti-double-charge guarantee at the database level.
annotations.title: @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) + @Query

annotations.body: Persists enums as readable strings (CARD, PENDING, DEAD) instead of fragile ordinals. All status columns use it.
annotations.why: Adding a new enum value never corrupts existing rows — ordinals would.
annotations.title: @Enumerated(STRING)

annotations.body: Triggers validation on request bodies. Every POST validates before any service code runs; failures become 400 via the advice.
annotations.why: Bad input (bad email, short PAN, non-https webhook URL) is rejected at the edge.
annotations.title: @Valid + constraints

annotations.body: Luhn checksum on card numbers plus @Pattern for PAN/CVV shapes and a custom @ExpiryYear validator. Vault input is the most guarded in the system.
annotations.why: Fake card numbers die before encryption — no junk in the vault.
annotations.title: @LuhnCheck + @ExpiryYear

annotations.body: Generates DTO↔entity mapping code at compile time. componentModel=SPRING makes mappers injectable; @Mapping handles renames and secret fields.
annotations.why: Entities (with secrets, audit, Money embeds) never leak onto the wire; zero hand-written mapping.
annotations.title: @Mapper + @Mapping

annotations.body: Generates constructors, getters, builders, loggers. @RequiredArgsConstructor is the DI style everywhere; @Builder builds test/entity objects; @Slf4j gives log.
annotations.why: Removes ~40% boilerplate; constructor injection makes dependencies explicit and testable.

patterns.problem: Per-method charge logic (CARD/UPI/NETBANKING) isolated — new method = new @Component, no if/else in the service.
patterns.title: Strategy (payment processors)

patterns.problem: Single Map.get(method) lookup that fails fast if unregistered — one choke point for both internal and gateway dispatch.
patterns.title: Router ×2

patterns.problem: Hides heterogeneous bank/PSP APIs behind one PaymentResult — the service never touches provider SDKs.
patterns.title: Adapter (gateway)

patterns.problem: Composable per-request pipeline: JWT for dashboards, API-key+HMAC for merchant APIs, idempotency replay — ordered chains, stateless sessions.
patterns.title: Filter chain

patterns.problem: Event row saved in the SAME transaction as the payment — Kafka can be down at write time and nothing is lost; poller relays at-least-once.
patterns.title: Transactional Outbox

patterns.problem: Merchant endpoints flap — 7 attempts over 1m→24h on a Redis time-ordered queue, DB reconcile heals lost entries, virtual threads deliver.
patterns.title: Retry with backoff

patterns.problem: Poison/undeliverable events park in dlq_event (REQUIRES_NEW) for audit/replay instead of retrying forever.
patterns.title: Dead-letter queue

patterns.problem: Illegal jumps (capture before authorize) throw InvalidStateTransitionException; every move is audit-logged with actor.
patterns.title: State machine

patterns.problem: Entities never touch the wire — secrets, audit fields and Money embeds stay server-side.
patterns.title: DTO + Mapper

patterns.problem: API-key lookups hit Redis (5-min TTL) not Postgres+BCrypt per request; revoke/rotate explicitly evicts.
patterns.title: Cache-aside

patterns.problem: Request-scoped merchant holder instead of ThreadLocal — safe on virtual threads, read by filters and services.
patterns.title: Request-scoped context

patterns.problem: Pessimistic row lock serializes concurrent capture/callback on one payment — no double-capture.
patterns.title: Pessimistic locking
